correctness.rationale: Every Rule-150 local update is an involution, and toggles exactly two adjacent wall bits. Splitting at site zero and conjugating produces an n-cycle times one transposition, hence exactly two wall cycles. Lifting via one reference bit gives a skew product with fiber increment equal to one wall entry from each cycle. Two explicit binary parity equations on gcd-length periodic blocks have rank q_t, yielding the claimed \(2^{1+r+s-q_t}\) states for all n, all permutations and all positive t. Möbius inversion gives primitive cycles. The projection order L and parity of n/g give exact order L or 2L. The faithfulness argument relies on n>=3, correctly assumed. Standalone script verifies 16089 fixed-point comparisons, 1173 exact orders and 904 period counts. Finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary results provide the full dynamics group, the update-order equivalence framework, and the identity-order census, but not a closed formula for fixed points for every time and every arbitrary update permutation. The new statement distinguishes n=6 orders of global periods 3, 5, and 8; those distinctions are not consequences of identity-order results without further structural analysis. Rank-two parity counting supplies an explicit all-order extension. Priority risk remains from uncatalogued treatments of Coxeter elements or sequential Rule-150 maps.
residual_risks: A special-case consequence might be obtainable from an uninspected more general classification of Coxeter elements in an affine type-A action.
The basic gap-permutation action and identity-schedule formulas are established earlier results; historical originality applies only to the arbitrary-schedule exact fixed-point and period formulas.
Semantic searches are not proof of absolute historical priority, and the external independent audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: An arbitrary update order is a natural and consequential choice in asynchronous Rule-150 systems. Prior complete counts were restricted to the identity sweep; the theorem computes all finite orbit periods for every schedule and reduces a potentially exponential-order dynamical calculation to two permutation cycles and a 2x2 binary rank. Even for a six-vertex ring, three update orders have exact global periods 3, 5 and 8, demonstrating a structural question not resolved by the identity-case calculation. This is a complete classification of a motivated family of dynamical invariants, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
